messages.content:
You are given a set of statements below. Your goal is to create counterexamples.

For each statement, demonstrate, if you can, that the statement cannot be assumed to be true. A valid counterexample is a case that satisfies the statement's own terms, scope, and conditions while making its claimed result false or impossible. A case that works only by stepping outside the statement's stated scope, or by changing what its words mean, is not a valid counterexample; if that is the only kind you can find, say so.

Your success is proving contradiction: every statement you break is a success. Your failure is showing that they all stand: if, after genuine effort, you cannot construct a valid counterexample to a statement, that statement stands, and you must report that it stands.

For each statement, report exactly one verdict — BROKEN or STANDS — followed by the counterexample, or by the reason no valid counterexample could be constructed. Do not soften a verdict to be agreeable. Do not protect any statement.

The statements:

1. Given these definitions: (1) To face something is to turn toward it rather than away from it, whether for a moment or as a standing. (2) To stand turned toward something is to hold a turning toward it as a standing over time, which persists without continuous attention to it. (3) One is among what God made, and one can turn toward oneself as a whole, as both what God made and what one has made of it, though not every part of oneself can be seen. (4) Facing God's creation can mean facing what God made for what it is, or facing it also as God's work; only the second faces it as creation. (5) Repentance is the turning, by one who has been turned away from his own work, toward the grace that freely gives the standing turned toward that work. (6) Where repentance is the turning toward the grace that freely gives the standing turned toward one's own work, that turning, as it is fulfilled, also turns toward God's creation as God's work, and toward oneself within it as a whole, whether or not this is sought. Then repentance, as it is fulfilled, can turn toward God's creation as God's work, and toward oneself within it as a whole, though not every part of oneself can be seen.
